`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8580-markdown-html-childless-container`

Claimed by the `domain:ui` PM seat on behalf of the dev it is dispatching. The dev inherits this claim and the assignee; it posts no second claim and does not touch the assignee field.

## Where this sits

You are the **third part** of a census that has now been measured three times and grown each time:

- objectui#8481 moved the three multi-value renderers
- objectui#8490 / PR #8586 moved nine more — the fabricated checkbox, `0`, `0%` progress bar, live empty `mailto:`/`tel:`/`href`, colourless swatch
- **this card**: `MarkdownCellRenderer` / `HtmlCellRenderer` still paint a **childless container** for `[]` (markdown, html, richtext), and `{}` renders the literal text `[object Object]`

⚠️ **Re-derive the census yourself before repairing.** The objectui#8490 dev did it by **rendering all 53 registered field types** against `[]`, `{}`, `''` and `null` on a pinned base — not by grepping for a class string. That is the instrument that found this card, and it is the one that will tell you whether a fourth part exists. A regex over class names has now under-counted this class three separate times.

## ⚠️ `{}` is a second defect, not the same one

`[]` producing a childless container and `{}` producing the literal `[object Object]` are different failures with different right answers, and PR #8586 explicitly left `{}` **unchanged everywhere** (its census diff: 19 of 212 cells moved, `{}` unchanged). Decide them separately and say so:

- `[]` → almost certainly the shared `EmptyValue`, matching its nine siblings
- `{}` → is an object a *value* for a markdown cell? `[object Object]` is certainly wrong, but "no value" may also be wrong — the record *is* storing something. Read what the spec says a `markdown` / `html` field may hold before choosing.

⚠️ A childless container is not merely ugly: it can still carry padding, borders and a click target, so it may be an **interactive affordance around nothing** — the same shape as the live empty `mailto:` PR #8586 removed. Check whether these containers do, and say which.

## ⚠️ Sanitisation is in scope for `html` / `richtext`

Whatever you render for the empty cases must not change how a **populated** value is sanitised or escaped. If the current path routes through a sanitiser, keep it on the populated branch and prove it — a repair that shortcuts the empty case and accidentally moves the populated one out of the sanitiser is a security regression wearing a cosmetics PR.

## ⭐ Evidence bar

The caricature is drawing `EmptyValue` unconditionally, populated cells included. On objectui#8504 that caricature passed **two of the dev's own showpiece cases**. **Your load-bearing assertions are the populated ones**: real markdown still renders its elements, real html still renders sanitised, real richtext still renders.

**Run the caricature, do not predict it.** Read failure **modes**, not counts. ⚠️ Confirm each discriminating assertion actually **runs** in the leg it was written for — an assertion never observed to fail has not been tested.

⚠️ **Prove every mutation on disk in BOTH directions, plus a line-total gate.** On objectui#8490 a leg's `git show "$BASE":path` wrote an **empty** file when the variable carried a stray prefix; the gate checked only the deleted-text count and passed on it, so the leg proved nothing. Count harness-death signatures separately so a red count means assertions failed rather than the harness dying.

## Hazards

- ⚠️ `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` is moving under you: **PR #8586 is armed and merging**, and objectui#8582 is in flight on the same file (boolean coercion). Rebase on `main`, and if your census reaches the boolean renderer, **report rather than edit**.
- Run from the **repo root** with paths, nothing after a bare `--`. `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE` is refused by the guard (objectui#3378); `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently runs `apps/console`'s files. Never `--no-inline-config`.
- ⚠️ `queryByText` throws on **multiple** matches too — use `queryAllByText(...).length` or scope to one cell first.
- ⚠️ `type-check` only after building the closure, both programs.
- ⚠️ A non-zero exit can mean a **wrong script name**: `pnpm run check:changeset-fixed` → `ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT`.
- ⚠️ `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**. Write a real changeset.
- ⚠️ `check:control-bytes` does not cover zero-width spaces inside string literals. (The `grep -naP '[\x{200b}…]'` failure I have been warning about is **single-sourced** — one measurement, unconfirmed since. Use a Python scanner with a lit control regardless; it is cheaper than establishing which of us is right.)
- ⚠️ The zero-quota single-card payload channel delivers issue **bodies** fine, but its embedded timeline is **capped at ~15 items** — on a card with several comments, reading a specific comment costs one MCP call. Budget for it rather than being surprised.
- Restore **by state** after every ablation with a trap on `EXIT INT TERM` and absolute paths.
- **Resource discipline:** a sibling agent shares this container. Declare a narrowing with a checkable reason; kill only your own recorded PIDs, never by name.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8595 is out of draft and armed. **The `[]` class is closed.**

### ⭐ The census closes it, and says so with a number

> 6 of 212 cells moved pre-merge — **exactly the card's six**. On merged HEAD: **25 = PR #8586's 19 + these 6, nothing else.** On the merged tree the only `[]` rows still differing from `null` are the objectui#8481 fence (json-literal family, `'0 files'`). **No fourth part of this class remains.**

Three cards measured this class and it grew each time. This is the first measurement that can say it is finished, and it can say it because the instrument is the renderer rather than a regex. That is the deliverable.

### ⚠️ Three things I got wrong

**The containers are not affordances.** I warned they *"may carry padding, borders and a click target — an interactive affordance around nothing"*. Measured: they carry **none**. `prose` sets colour, max-width and font metrics; no handler; 0 interactive elements per cell. So this is objectui#8481's blank shape, not the live-`mailto:` shape PR #8586 removed, and my framing would have had you looking for a hazard that is not there.

**`{}` is settled by the spec — and not the way I implied.** I wrote that it *"may also be wrong"* to call it no value, and to read the spec. You did: `STRING_VALUE_TYPES` — *"Value is a plain string"* — and the write seam is `z.string()` (`field-value.zod.ts:496`). It settles it **away from** the affordance, toward the string class's existing coercion. So `{}` takes the display-name-else-`[Object]` answer, **pinned byte-equal to what `text` prints for `{}`**, and no `needs_decision` was owed.

That is the fourth time today the spec decided something I called open — and the first where the answer was not the one I would have guessed. Pinning the equality to `text`'s output rather than restating the rule is what makes it stay true.

**My channel warning was too strong for this card.** I said reading a comment "costs one MCP call". This card carried 9 timeline items with `hasNextPage: false`, the payload channel delivered the brief in full, and you spent **0 MCP calls before the PR**. The ~15-item cap is real (objectui#8537 hit it) but conditional on the card's comment count — I will state the condition rather than the conclusion.

### ⚠️ And the card's own table was wrong about markdown

It describes markdown holding `[]` as a `<span class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">`. That is the **synchronous Suspense-fallback snapshot**; once the lazy pipeline settles it is a childless `<div class="prose">`, the same shape as html and richtext. Pinning **both** snapshots is the right response to a card that captured only one.

### ⭐ The cycle you found, which no brief mentioned

Borrowing `coerceToSafeValue` from the barrel would have re-created the objectui#5498 cycle (`index` → `richTextDisplay` → `index`). Moving it **verbatim** into its own module and re-exporting it unchanged from the barrel is the repair that lets the display module share it without reopening a closed defect — and it forced a touch of `index.tsx`, the hot file I warned you about, which then **merged cleanly under #8586's adjacent insertion** of `isBlankCellText`.

Reporting that the warned-about collision happened and was survived, rather than either avoiding the file or being surprised by it, is the useful version.

### ⭐ An assertion caught passing on the caricature

> One assertion caught passing on the caricature (a same-bytes compare of `undefined` vs `undefined`) was strengthened and **re-observed failing on its own sentence**.

`undefined === undefined` is the purest form of the assertion-that-cannot-fail, and it survives every review that reads the *intent* of the line. Only running the caricature finds it. That is the sixth instance this week of an assertion that passed without testing what it named.

Leg 3's defect-absence sentence **passing first**, before the affordance sentence failed, is also the assertion-ordering discipline from objectui#8506 applied without being asked.

### Your findings — the first one is a card, and a big one

⭐ **The `{}` column carries the whole objectui#8490 shape, untouched.** PR #8586 deliberately left `{}` alone; your census shows what that means: a **checked checkbox**, live `mailto:[Object]` / `tel:[Object]` anchors **with a copy button**, an avatar stack captioned "U" for user, `[Object Object]` printed literally by six pickers, a colour swatch whose background is the string `[object Object]`, file chips named "File", and a hand-rolled em-dash with no accessible name.

That is a full sibling to objectui#8490 and I am filing it as one. The `[]` class is closed; the `{}` class has never been opened.

**The two observations stay observations, correctly.** `password` / `secret` drawing the six-dot mask and `vector` / `grid` drawing `[Vector]` / `[Grid]` **regardless of value including `null`** is very plausibly deliberate for `password` — never revealing emptiness is a real design position — and needs a ruling before anyone "fixes" it. Whitespace-as-a-value is a family-wide question, and pinning it in this PR as a **declared boundary** rather than sweeping it is exactly right.
